prompt.text:
A friend looked after your home and your pet while you were away on holiday.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• thank your friend for their help
• tell them about your holiday
• offer to do something for them in return

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

stimulus.situation: A friend looked after your home and your pet while you were away on holiday.
points: thank your friend for their help
offer to do something for them in return

response_text:
Dear Sam,

I just wanted to say a huge thank you for looking after the flat and Biscuit while I was away. I know how busy you've been at work, so it really means a lot. Biscuit clearly had a great time with you – he's been sulking ever since I got back!

The holiday was fantastic. We spent the first few days in Lisbon, wandering around the old town and eating far too many custard tarts, and then took the train down to the coast. The beaches were almost empty because it was the end of the season, and the water was still warm enough to swim. The highlight was a boat trip along the cliffs, where we saw dolphins swimming right next to us. I'll show you the photos when we meet.

Anyway, I'd love to return the favour. You mentioned that you're going to visit your parents in December, so why don't I water your plants and collect your post while you're away? And let me take you out for dinner next weekend – my treat, of course.

Let me know when you're free.

Lots of love,
Maria

criteria.summary: This is a complete, well-judged letter to a friend. The purpose is clear from the first sentence, and all three points are fully developed with relevant detail: the thanks come with a personal touch, the holiday is described with specific places and events, and the offers are concrete and linked to your friend's plans. The informal tone is consistent from the opening to the closing and suits the situation. I found nothing irrelevant or missing.

The letter is very easy to follow. It moves from thanks, to the holiday, to the offer, and ends with a short close that asks for a reply. Each paragraph has one clear job, and the breaks fall where the letter moves on. Links are natural and unobtrusive, for example 'Anyway, I'd love to return the favour', 'so why don't I...' and 'And let me take you out'. Reference words such as 'it' and 'there' are used accurately, and nothing needs re-reading. No slips in organisation or linking stand out.

The vocabulary is natural, precise and well suited to an informal letter to a friend. Phrases such as "return the favour", "my treat, of course", "wandering around the old town" and "the highlight was a boat trip along the cliffs" are idiomatic and collocate well. Descriptions are specific (custard tarts, dolphins, empty beaches at the end of the season) and the wording is varied. No spelling, word-formation or word-choice errors are noticeable, so the only thing keeping it from the top level is that the range, while fluent, rarely goes beyond everyday vocabulary.

Your letter uses a wide range of structures with full control: time clauses, reason clauses, relative clauses, a reported statement and a 'why don't I' suggestion are all used correctly. Punctuation is accurate, including the dashes, commas and apostrophes. I could not find any grammar or punctuation errors, and the sentences read naturally for an informal letter.
